Abstract
•  Olist marketplace orders span 2016–2018.
•  Nine CSV files feed a normalized MySQL database.
•  Ten SQL reports explain orders, revenue and delivery.
•  A custom local website provides filters and order details.
•  Charts, exact values and exports support review.
•  A five-minute cache speeds repeated requests.

Introduction
•  Marketplace records span several related files.
•  Manual joins make analysis slow and inconsistent.
•  Operations users need delivery and revenue comparisons.
•  Objectives: clean data, enforce keys and build ten reports.
•  The dashboard connects report results to filters and exports.

Scope and Methodology
•  Historical Brazilian orders, payments, deliveries and reviews.
•  Analytics uses MySQL queries against the imported dataset.
•  The project excludes checkout and real-time processing.
•  Inspect, clean and import source files.
•  Validate SQL results, then present charts and exports.

Problem Identification and Analysis
•  Nine linked CSV files complicate consistent analysis.
•  Geolocation repeats zip prefixes. Review identifiers may repeat.
•  Undelivered orders can have missing delivery dates.
•  Operations users need state, timing and revenue comparisons.
•  Normalized storage supports consistent joins and constraints.
Template: CAPSTONE PP TEMPLATE.pdf. Source content: CAPSTONE REVIEW 1.pptx. Project updates verified against current SQL and WEBPAGE files and local MySQL results. Dataset period: 2016–2018.
Solution Design and Implementation
•  Schema and repeatable CSV import.
•  SQL views and ten parameterized report queries.
•  Python HTTP endpoints validate filters and query MySQL.
•  HTML, CSS and JavaScript render the custom website.
•  A bounded cache reuses identical requests for five minutes.
Template: CAPSTONE PP TEMPLATE.pdf. Source content: CAPSTONE REVIEW 1.pptx. Project updates verified against current SQL and WEBPAGE files and local MySQL results. Dataset period: 2016–2018.
System Architecture
•  Data source: nine Olist CSV files
•  Storage: nine normalized MySQL tables
•  Analysis: two views and ten report queries
•  Service: Python HTTP server with in-memory cache
•  Interface: Overview, Orders, Reports and Database
•  Output: charts, exact values, CSV, Excel and PDF

title: On-time and late deliveries by state

text:
SELECT sub.state, sub.delivery_outcome, sub.cnt
FROM (
    SELECT vdp.state, vdp.delivery_outcome, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM v_delivery_performance vdp
    WHERE vdp.delivery_outcome IN ('on_time', 'late')
      AND (%(start_date)s IS NULL OR vdp.order_purchase_timestamp >= %(start_date)s)
      AND (%(end_date)s IS NULL OR vdp.order_purchase_timestamp < %(end_date)s)
    GROUP BY vdp.state, vdp.delivery_outcome
) sub
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT vdp2.state
    FROM v_delivery_performance vdp2
    WHERE vdp2.delivery_outcome IN ('on_time', 'late')
      AND (%(start_date)s IS NULL OR vdp2.order_purchase_timestamp >= %(start_date)s)
      AND (%(end_date)s IS NULL OR vdp2.order_purchase_timestamp < %(end_date)s)
    GROUP BY vdp2.state
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500
) qualified ON qualified.state = sub.state
ORDER BY sub.state, sub.delivery_outcome

R07 · undefined
•  undefined

SELECT ranked.category_name_en, ranked.total_revenue, ranked.rnk
FROM (
    SELECT COALESCE(pc.category_name_en, pc.category_name, 'unknown') AS category_name_en,
           SUM(oi.price) AS total_revenue,
           RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(oi.price) DESC) AS rnk
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN product_categories pc ON pc.category_name = p.category_name
    WHERE (%(start_date)s IS NULL OR o.order_purchase_timestamp >= %(start_date)s)
      AND (%(end_date)s IS NULL OR o.order_purchase_timestamp < %(end_date)s)
      AND (%(state)s IS NULL OR EXISTS (
              SELECT 1 FROM customers c
              JOIN geolocation g ON g.zip_prefix = c.zip_prefix
              WHERE c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND g.state = %(state)s
           ))
    GROUP BY COALESCE(pc.category_name_en, pc.category_name, 'unknown')
) ranked
WHERE ranked.rnk <= 10
ORDER BY ranked.rnk

SELECT g.state, ROUND(AVG(oi.freight_value), 2) AS avg_freight
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN geolocation g ON g.zip_prefix = c.zip_prefix
WHERE (%(start_date)s IS NULL OR o.order_purchase_timestamp >= %(start_date)s)
  AND (%(end_date)s IS NULL OR o.order_purchase_timestamp < %(end_date)s)
  AND (%(category)s IS NULL OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM products p
          WHERE p.product_id = oi.product_id AND p.category_name = %(category)s
       ))
GROUP BY g.state
ORDER BY avg_freight DESC

SELECT CASE
        WHEN vdp.delivery_days BETWEEN 0 AND 7 THEN '0-7 days'
        WHEN vdp.delivery_days BETWEEN 8 AND 14 THEN '8-14 days'
        WHEN vdp.delivery_days BETWEEN 15 AND 21 THEN '15-21 days'
        WHEN vdp.delivery_days BETWEEN 22 AND 30 THEN '22-30 days'
        WHEN vdp.delivery_days BETWEEN 31 AND 45 THEN '31-45 days'
        ELSE '46+ days'
       END AS delivery_bucket,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM v_delivery_performance vdp
WHERE vdp.delivery_days IS NOT NULL
  AND (%(start_date)s IS NULL OR vdp.order_purchase_timestamp >= %(start_date)s)
  AND (%(end_date)s IS NULL OR vdp.order_purchase_timestamp < %(end_date)s)
  AND (%(state)s IS NULL OR vdp.state = %(state)s)
GROUP BY delivery_bucket
ORDER BY MIN(vdp.delivery_days)

title: Average review score by delivery outcome

text:
SELECT vdp.delivery_outcome,
       ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
       COUNT(*) AS review_count
FROM order_reviews r
JOIN v_delivery_performance vdp ON vdp.order_id = r.order_id
WHERE vdp.delivery_outcome IN ('on_time', 'late')
  AND (%(start_date)s IS NULL OR vdp.order_purchase_timestamp >= %(start_date)s)
  AND (%(end_date)s IS NULL OR vdp.order_purchase_timestamp < %(end_date)s)
  AND (%(state)s IS NULL OR vdp.state = %(state)s)
GROUP BY vdp.delivery_outcome
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC
